facts.statement: The dorsal margin of the maxilla in Sinotyrannus is unusually concave, unlike the convex condition found in tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The dorsal margin of the maxilla is unusually concave unlike the convex condition in tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The three preserved vertebrae of Sinotyrannus have very tall neural spines.
facts.quote: The three preserved vertebrae have very tall neural spines.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago during the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 120 million years ago durante el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus is known from a single fossil skeleton including a partial skull from the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Sinotyrannus es conocido por un solo esqueleto fósil que incluye un cráneo parcial, proviene de la Formación Jiufotang del Cretácico Inferior en Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus was much larger than contemporary tyrannosauroids, reaching between 7.5 and 10 meters in length, making it the largest theropod in the Jiufotang Formation biota of Jehol.
facts.quote: Es por mucho más grande que los tiranosauroideos contemporáneos, llegando a medir entre 7,5 y 10 metros, siendo de esta manera el terópodo más grande de la de la Formación Jiufotang en la biota de Jehol.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus lived in a wet environment characterized by well-watered forests and large lakes.
facts.quote: Sinotyrannus lived in a rather wet environment with well-watered forests and large lakes.

facts.statement: The environment where Sinotyrannus lived was prone to high levels of volcanism.
facts.quote: Despite this, the area was quite prone to high volcanism.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus is classified within the family Proceratosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Proceratosauridae

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that Sinotyrannus, known from an adult specimen, may be a mature form of the earlier named genus Huaxiagnathus, which is known only from immature specimens.
facts.quote: Cau and Paterna used an updated version of this dataset to deduce that Sinotyrannus—known from a specimen of an adult individual—was a mature form of the "compsognathid" Huaxiagnathus, which is known only from two immature specimens.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus is among the largest basal tyrannosauroids known, challenging the previous assumption that tyrannosauroids gradually increased in size from small basal forms to advanced apex predators like Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: It is among the largest basal tyrannosauroids known, repudiating the previously presumed trend that tyrannosauroids gradually increased in size throughout the Cretaceous period from small basal forms like Dilong to advanced apex predators such as Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The specific epithet refers to the Kazuo district in Liaoning.
facts.quote: El epíteto específico se refiere al distrito de Kazuo en Liaoning.

facts.statement: The holotype KZV-001 is a disarticulated partial skeleton including the front of the skull, three dorsal vertebrae, an incomplete ilium, three articulated hand phalanges including a claw, and other fragmentary bones.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Sinotyrannus, KZV-001, un esqueleto parcial desarticulado que incluye la parte frontal del cráneo, tres vértebras dorsales, el ilion incompleto, tres falanges manuales articuladas, incluida una ungueal y otros huesos fragmentarios.

facts.statement: In 2016, its size was revised to a smaller length of 7.5 meters and weight of 1.2 tons.
facts.quote: En 2016 se le dio un tamaño más pequeño de 7,5 metros y 1,2 toneladas.

facts.statement: The dorsal margin of the maxilla is unusually concave, differing from the convex condition found in tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: El margen dorsal del maxilar es inusualmente cóncavo a diferencia de la condición convexa de los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: Its large, elliptical nostrils support its relationship with the Proceratosauridae family.
facts.quote: Las narinas son grandes y elípticas, lo que respalda su relación con los Proceratosauridae.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus may have had a high nasal crest like other proceratosaurids, though insufficient nasal bones are preserved to be certain.
facts.quote: Sinotyrannus podría haber tenido una cresta nasal alta como otros proceratosáuridos, aunque no se conservan suficientes nasales para estar seguros.

facts.statement: The three preserved vertebrae have very high neural spines.
facts.quote: Las tres vértebras conservadas tienen espinas neurales muy altas.

facts.statement: The ilia are preserved mainly as natural molds, with the external mold of the left ilium being the most complete.
facts.quote: Los ilion se presentan principalmente como moldes, siendo el molde del lado externo del ilion izquierdo el más completo.

facts.statement: The preacetabular blade is short and wide with a massive pubic peduncle, while the postacetabular blade is longer and thinner with a triangular ischial peduncle.
facts.quote: La hoja preacetabular es corta y ancha, con un pedúnculo púbico masivo, mientras que la hoja postacetabular es más larga y delgada, con un pedúnculo isquiático triangular.

facts.statement: Sinotyrannus was among the largest known basal tyrannosauroids, refuting the previously assumed trend that tyrannosauroids gradually increased in size from small basal forms like Dilong to advanced apex predators like Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Sinotyrannus estaba entre los tiranosauroides basales más grandes conocidos, refutando la tendencia previamente supuesta de que los tiranosauroides aumentaron gradualmente de tamaño a lo largo del período Cretácico desde pequeñas formas basales como Dilong hasta depredadores de ápice avanzados como Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The original description suggested it might be the oldest tyrannosaur due to its large size, but later analyses place it as a proceratosaurid tyrannosaur.
facts.quote: La descripción original de Sinotyrannus proponía que podría haber sido el tiranosáurido más antiguo debido a su gran tamaño, pero análisis posteriores lo sitúan como un tiranosáurido proceratosáurido.

facts.statement: Conversely, a 2016 analysis placed Juratyrant and Stokesosaurus outside Proceratosauridae and proposed that Sinotyrannus is a sister taxon to Yutyrannus within Proceratosauridae.
facts.quote: En cambio, un análisis de 2016 colocó a Juratyrant y Stokesosaurus fuera de los Proceratosauridae y propuso que Sinotyrannus es un taxón hermano de Yutyrannus dentro de Proceratosauridae.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Proceratosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Proceratosauridae

facts.statement: Its family is Proceratosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Proceratosauridae

facts.statement: The type species is Sinotyrannus kazuoensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Sinotyrannus kazuoensis

facts.statement: Its time range is from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago, during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
